$comment: Works switched off, one entry per work id. Their text is not built, and the
addresses that would have shown it redirect to the source instead.
WHAT THIS IS FOR: quality. A work whose parse is damaged — text missing,
paragraphs swallowed by a source-HTML defect — is worse than a work we
don't publish at all, because a reader has no way to tell that what they
are reading is incomplete. Entries here are expected to be TEMPORARY: the
fix is to repair the parser and remove the entry.
It is also the lever if a rights holder ever asks us to stop publishing one
work — but nobody has, and this file is not the shape of the request the
copyright posture actually anticipates (see the note at the end).
FIELDS: both are notes to US, not to readers. Nothing here is shown on the
site; the site is only told WHICH ids are off (scripts/sync-corpus.mjs
writes the id list, and nothing else, into the index tier).
date    ISO date the work was switched off.
reason  Free text. Be specific — 'missing ~41% of its paragraphs to the
source-HTML defect in docs/research/vatican-documents.md §7.1' is
what tells the next person whether the entry can go; 'quality
issues' is not.
WHAT AN ENTRY DOES: everything derived from the work stops being written
into the build — reading text AND structure tree (scripts/sync-corpus.mjs).
A table of contents built from a parse we do not trust is not better than
nothing, and the addresses enumerated from it would point at text that was
never written. The manifest still goes into the index, because that is what
lets a listing fall back to another edition of the same document.
WHAT THE READER GETS: the source page. A document still readable in its
other language is listed and read here in that one; a document with no
readable edition left keeps its row and its address, and going there sends
the reader to vatican.va (documents/[slug]/+page.ts). Nothing on the site
says a word about it — no badge, no notice, no page explaining the absence.
The same redirect covers a work whose parse simply produced nothing, with
no entry in this file: from where the reader stands the two are one event.
The site used to render a notice here naming the work and quoting the
reason below; it was removed on 2026-08-24 (docs/decisions.md).
Keyed by WORK ID ('encyclical.humanae-vitae.pt'), not slug, because parse
damage is usually per-edition: a document's PT edition can be broken while
its EN one is clean, and switching off both would throw away a good text to
hide a bad one. Six of the eight documents with an entry today are complete
in their other language and are read there normally.
ON THE RIGHTS CASE, HONESTLY: this is per-work, and a takedown from the
Holy See would not be. Essentially the whole corpus outside the two Bible
editions is Libreria Editrice Vaticana material, so such a request would
concern most of the site at once — a whole-site decision (stop publishing,
or degrade everything to link-outs), not a handful of entries here. This
file is not that lever and should not be mistaken for one. See
docs/decisions.md §Posture.
